segments.text: Luke and Manny play on the same basketball team, and their coach is awful. He spends the game screaming at the kids and calling them stupid. Phil tries to talk to him calmly, but Jay jumps in, threatens to throw a shoe at his head, and the coach quits on the spot.

Phil tries to talk to him calmly, but Jay jumps in, threatens to throw a shoe at his head, and the coach quits on the spot.

segments.text: Before leaving, he tells Jay to coach the team himself.
segments.tts_text: [a storyteller building gentle suspense] Before leaving, he tells Jay to coach the team himself.

segments.text: Phil has actually coached basketball before and expects Jay to hand the team over. Jay does the opposite. He makes himself head coach, gives Phil the assistant job, and tells the boys to play more aggressively. It goes badly.

segments.text: The kids get confused, start fighting their own teammates for the ball, and the score gets worse while Jay ignores Phil’s advice.

segments.text: Phil finally tells Jay what’s bothering him. Jay keeps taking over whenever Phil is doing something, whether it’s coaching basketball or grilling steaks at a barbecue. Phil wants him to admit that there are some things Phil is simply better at.

segments.text: Jay hates saying it, but eventually he gives Phil the team. Phil draws up one simple play to get Manny his first shot of the season. Manny almost makes it. They still lose, but at least the boys finally look like a team instead of a small riot.

segments.text: Later the two mothers compare notes while babysitting Lily. Claire gets revenge when Alex asks for money to go out: she gives it to her, then loudly talks about her “little boobies” and buying a training bra in front of everyone. Gloria is subtler.

segments.text: Jay introduces Mitchell to Charlie Bingham, a wealthy businessman who offers him an environmental-law job. At Charlie’s house, Mitchell and Cameron finally admit what they actually want: Mitchell wants to work, and Cameron wants to stay home.

segments.text: They agree Mitchell should take the job, then lock themselves in the garage. Trying to get out, they keep pressing the controls for Charlie’s driveway turntable and repeatedly smash their car into his Ferrari.
